title: Rig two cardioid mics on a stereo bar as an ORTF pair aimed at the choir
instruction: Rig the two small cardioid microphones on the stereo bar as an ORTF pair for the choir on the riser. The silver grille end of each mic is its capsule. Lay both mics flat on the grey bar plate, set the way an ORTF pair is set, aimed at the centre of the choir (the white mark on the riser), then let go of both mics.
context: Location and broadcast recording engineers (sound engineering technicians, O*NET 27-4014) rig stereo microphone pairs for choirs, orchestras and services. ORTF, the near-coincident technique of the French broadcaster Office de Radiodiffusion-Television Francaise, is one of the standard set-ups (Eargle, The Microphone Book; the Schoeps and DPA guides): two cardioid microphones with their capsules 17 cm apart and their axes splayed outward at 110 degrees, the pair centred on the source and aimed at its centre. Spacing and angle together give a recording angle of about 96 degrees. Engineers check a rigged pair with a ruler and a protractor: a pair set up parallel, as an XY pair at 90 degrees, with crossed capsules or off the source's centre gives a different stereo image. Here the instruction names the technique only: the robot must know what an ORTF pair is, tell each mic's capsule end and set both mics to it, at full scale.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Headings are seen from above, counter-clockwise from +x. Everything except the two microphones is fixed to the table. (1) Stereo-bar plate: a grey aluminium plate, 80 mm (x) by 280 mm (y), 8 mm thick, spanning x 26.0-34.0 cm and y -14.0 to +14.0 cm (centred on the midline). (2) Choir riser: a dark-blue painted wooden block, 30 mm (x) by 300 mm (y), 40 mm tall, spanning x 47.0-50.0 cm and y -15.0 to +15.0 cm. On its top, a white plastic disc 12 mm across and 0.5 mm thick, glued on, centred at x 48.5 cm, y 0 (the centre of the choir), and six singer figures, maroon-painted wooden pegs 16 mm across and 30 mm tall, standing at x 48.5 cm and y -12, -8, -4, +4, +8 and +12 cm. The source axis is the line y 0 through the white mark. (3) Two case pads: grey foam sheets 100 x 50 mm, 1 mm thick, one centred at x 25.0 cm, y +32.0 cm with its long side turned 20 degrees clockwise from x, the other centred at x 25.0 cm, y -32.0 cm turned 20 degrees anticlockwise. (4) Two microphones, loose and alike: small pencil-condenser stand-ins, each a rigid block 70 mm long and 24 x 24 mm across, 80 g (a hollow aluminium case). Its rear 55 mm is the matte-black body; its front 15 mm is a silver steel-mesh grille, the capsule end. Each lies flat (a 70 x 24 mm face down) centred in a case pad and along it: mic A at x 25.0 cm, y +32.0 cm, its grille end pointing 20 degrees clockwise of +x (toward the midline); mic B at x 25.0 cm, y -32.0 cm, its grille end pointing 20 degrees anticlockwise of +x. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from both mics' poses and both grippers (in a real trial: a steel rule, a protractor and a top photo). Each mic's capsule point c is the grille's centre, 7.5 mm behind its front face on the mic's axis, at mid-height; its axis u points from the tail to the grille end; distances and angles are seen from above. Gate: both mics let go, still and lying on the plate, else the score is 0. 'Let go': every gripper's fingers at least 10 mm from each mic (a gripper's fingers are taken as everything within reach of a pad's outer corner around the 38 mm stretch back from the point between its pad tips: half the finger gap plus 8 mm out, 13.5 mm across, whatever the gripper's heading). 'Still': in each of the last two 0.5 s the mic's centre travelled under 1.5 mm, and its heading changed less than 2 degrees over the last 1 s. 'On the plate': its long axis within 10 degrees of horizontal, its centre over the plate and its lowest point within 5 mm of the plate's top, so a mic lying on the other mic, on the table or held up fails. Then three checks. A (angle): the two axes 110 +/- 8 degrees apart, splayed outward (the capsules farther apart than the tails: (cA - cB) . (uA - uB) > 0, so a crossed pair fails), and the bisector uA + uB within 30 degrees of the direction from the capsules' midpoint to the white mark (facing the choir). S (spacing): the capsule points 170 +/- 10 mm apart. C (centred and aimed): the capsules' midpoint within 10 mm of the source axis (y 0) and the bisector within 5 degrees of the direction from the midpoint to the mark. First match wins: gate not met, 0; A and S and C, 1.0; A and S, 0.67; A (with or without C), 0.33; otherwise 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.33, 0.67, 1.0. Examples: 110 degrees and 170 mm with the midpoint 25 mm off the axis, or aimed 8 degrees off the mark, 0.67; 110 degrees with the capsules 130 mm apart, 0.33. Scoring 0: a parallel spaced pair, an XY pair (90 degrees, capsules together), a NOS pair (300 mm, 90 degrees), a DIN pair (200 mm, 90 degrees), the right angle crossed (capsules pointing across each other), a pair aimed away from the choir or sideways, a mic still in a gripper or still sliding, one mic laid across the other, the mics left in their pads. Either mic may be either one of the pair (swapping them changes nothing), and a mic rolled about its own axis scores the same. The trial ends early, at 1.0, once 1.0 has held for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit.
fidelity: Real pencil condensers are 100-150 mm round tubes held in clips on a stereo bar; here each is a 70 x 24 x 24 mm rigid block with a silver grille end, laid flat on a bar plate, and the choir is a riser block with a centre mark 16.5 cm beyond the capsules. Capsule spacing (170 mm) and angle (110 degrees) are full scale, as ORTF prescribes. Default simulator friction. The scorer reads only the mics' poses and the grippers' positions and openings.
reset_notes: Put mic A back flat in its grey case pad centred at x 25.0 cm, y +32.0 cm, along the pad, its silver grille end pointing 20 degrees clockwise of +x (toward the midline), and mic B in the other pad at x 25.0 cm, y -32.0 cm, its grille end pointing 20 degrees anticlockwise of +x. The plate, riser, mark, singer figures and pads are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
